sections.what: The Lighthouse of Houston provides low-vision health services, assistive technology, training and community programs. It also offers employment through business services and supports independent living. Our initial estimate combines a conditional health and training channel while using consolidated annual costs that eliminate internal transfers.
sections.monitoring: Request unique annual clients by service, completed training, incremental placements and retained net earnings against Texas Workforce Commission and other alternatives. Current website claims 25,000 people across programs and 58% blind or low-vision employment; the training page uses 60%, while the latest IRS describes 20,000 community services. These are different metrics and vintages, not additive unique beneficiaries.
sections.qualitative: Health, accessibility and work-resource pathways are relevant to blind and low-vision people. Current course descriptions identify training content, fees and public workforce referral alternatives. Consolidated audited accounts make it possible to avoid counting related-entity transfers twice. Service, activity and event totals are not a deduplicated clinical or job-placement cohort. Current employment shares do not establish additional jobs or earnings caused by donations. Whole consolidated cost versus the narrow modeled channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift estimate. The operating charity is EIN 74-1146781, distinct from related Foundation EIN 74-1618607. The consolidated audit includes related foundation and living centers; donations use the operating website. Internal grants and management fees are eliminated once.
sections.cost: The conditional annual partial-channel reference is $9.81 million per ten combined healthy-year welfare equivalents: 4.193652 clinical QALYs and 3.149499 signed resource equivalents. $10,000 corresponds to 0.010196 combined equivalents under proportional annual accounting, not demonstrated next-gift response. Full annual recognized recipient cost is $7,201,649. Judgments, not measured success: 1,000 distinct annual person/household proxies is a repeat-service mapping hypothesis, not the headline 25,000. Incremental response b=0.5 gives 500 exposed households. An 800-person clinical subgroup × b × response 0.4 gives 160 health responders, at 0.015 utility for two years after half a year delay. Of all 500, 15% achieve $4,000 one-year net work resources and $100 avoided medical spending; only positive components receive 0.75 overlap adjustment. Full $100 access burden and 0.0005 QALY harm remain on the union. Houston share is 0.95. Union 500 household proxies contains clinical subgroup 160; no separate clinical population is added. One welfare-equivalent adult per household at $25,000 annual consumption, with components netted before one log. Positive components alone receive overlap adjustment; negative components, all unavoidable costs and union harms remain full. Clinical failure retains resource exposures and burdens. ResourceYears is fraction of one year’s gain, not repeated lifetime payments. No retail medicines, gross salaries, ordinary survivor earnings or property wealth are counted. The $4,000 work-gain hypothesis is disposable earnings after tax, benefit withdrawal and recurring work expenses, not gross salary. Upfront tuition and foregone training time are separate cost components, not subtracted again from workGain. Central $100 access cost assumes referral funding; the full-tuition scenario instead charges $2,495 certification plus 150 training hours (five weeks at 30 hours) at a judged $15 per hour in foregone time, plus $100 access = $4,845 on every exposed household. The $15 opportunity cost is a judgment, not an observed wage or universal foregone earnings; referral versus self-pay and unpaid time differ. Displaced workers, employer or public-payer costs are tested separately. Training fees may already be paid by Texas Workforce Commission; no second charitable payment benefit is assumed. Central partner/payer zero is unknown-neutral, not observed zero or complete world net benefit. Other programs and external opportunity costs remain unknown; whole recipient cost versus this narrow channel is not complete portfolio EV or a marginal gift offer.
sections.funding: The official route supports the operating charity. Course fees and public referrals establish alternatives, not the price of an additional charitable placement; unrestricted donor response is unknown.

model.costScope: Full consolidated FY2025 expenses including merchandise costs and direct donor benefits, net of internal transfers, versus a partial health and training channel.
model.geographicAttribution: Greater Houston services with judged local share 0.95; consolidated living-center coverage may differ.
model.formula: Health = (clinicalN × unique × b × clinicalResponse × q × finite discounted duration − N × unique × b × union harm discounted at onset) × edition share. Income = signed joint household log welfare equivalents with positive-only overlap and full costs. Better-life cost = 10 × full annual cost / (health + income), only when combined benefits are positive.
model.counterfactual: Public workforce referrals, other vision providers, family support and alternative employment retained; net incremental resources only.
model.attribution: Annual incremental recipient response is distinct from cohort deduplication and geographic share; no claim of whole annual portfolio or marginal donation causal effect.
model.uncertainty: Source-grounded original cost/services; all causal mapping, utility and net resource priors unsupported. Complete portfolio and marginal donor EV unknown.
model.nativeOutcomes: Low-vision services, training courses and enterprise employment; not causal QALYs or incremental earnings.
